title: Overnight Sausage Strata
subtitle: Make-ahead bread, sausage, and egg bake rested overnight and baked hot.
description: Adapted from classic French strata tradition for firehall make-ahead breakfast: cubed bread layered with browned sausage and cheddar, soaked overnight in an egg-milk custard, then baked golden for ten crew portions.

ingredients.name: dry mustard
ingredients.notes: plus salt, pepper, and pinch nutmeg

ingredients.name: sliced green onions
ingredients.notes: plus hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Overnight Sausage Strata in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown sausage and build layers
steps.instruction: Cook sausage until no pink remains and internal temperature reaches 160°F; drain. Grease a deep 9x13 pan. Layer half the bread cubes, sausage, optional onion, and half the cheddar. Repeat layers. Plan about 20 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Mix and pour custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, mustard, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread layers, pressing gently so all cubes contact liquid. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Refrigerate overnight
steps.instruction: Cover tightly and refrigerate at least 8 hours or overnight so bread fully absorbs custard. Remove from fridge 30 minutes before baking to take the chill off the pan. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until puffed
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Top with remaining cheddar. Bake uncovered 45–50 minutes until center reaches 165°F, top is golden, and a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares so custard sets for clean portions. Garnish with green onions and serve with hot sauce at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assemble the night before so morning service is mostly oven time.
Use stale bread—fresh bread turns to mush after an overnight soak.
Check center temp with a probe; golden top can hide under-set custard in the middle.
cleanupNotes: Wash the assembly pan the morning of service while the strata bakes in the oven.
Discard any custard that spilled and baked onto the oven floor once cooled.
leftovers: Reheat portions covered at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Cube leftovers and pan-fry in butter for crispy strata hash with a fried egg on top.

Line up Overnight Sausage Strata on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.

mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Overnight Sausage Strata runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
